name: Risk Management Plan
one_liner: How this project will identify, assess and respond to risk.
purpose: Defines and documents the Risk Management Process for the project: how risks will be identified and assessed, what tools and techniques can be used, what the evaluation scales and tolerances are, the relevant roles and responsibilities, and how often risks need to be revisited. It also defines the risk monitoring and escalation process and the structure of the Risk Log. Risk management brings visibility to risks and accountability as to how they are handled.

fields.what: States what the plan does: outline the risk approach and process, identify risk roles and responsibilities, and specify the methodology, standards, tools and techniques supporting risk management.
fields.castor: Risk approach for Project CASTOR — €8.4 m, 26 months, mixed in-house and outsourced.

fields.what: Five objectives: risks identified, assessed, approved and reported; major risks reported to the Steering Layer; responses in line with risk appetite and thresholds; all risks controlled; actions effective.
fields.castor: No red risk may stay open without an approved response and a named owner.

fields.what: A four-step process — identification, assessment, response development, control — covering risks that may affect execution and the achievement of project objectives. Tailor or delete steps as needed.
fields.castor: Four steps kept unchanged; run weekly from the Executing Kick-off of 10 Jul 2026.

fields.what: Identify and document risks that can impact project objectives, using techniques focused on past trends or future exposure, bottom-up or top-down. New risks may arise at any point.
fields.castor: Initial 24-risk list built at the Planning Kick-off of 09 Apr 2026.

fields.what: Template default categories: Business; IT; People and organisation; External; Legal; Communication and Information. An organisational Risk Typology is used as reference where one exists.
fields.castor: All six kept; External covers Levallois Systems, Legal covers Treaty ratification.

fields.what: The guide lists the Risk Breakdown Structure among identification tools: a hierarchical decomposition of risk sources by category, the risk equivalent of a WBS. The template uses flat categories.
fields.castor: Two-level RBS: six categories, then sources — supplier, treaty, data migration, staffing.

fields.what: Assess the likelihood of each risk and the severity of its impact on project objectives. This assessment is necessary before any risk response can be planned; medium-to-high risks get priority.
fields.who: PM assesses · PCT and BM consulted
fields.castor: Assessment refreshed at every milestone, starting at the RfE gate of 03 Jul 2026.

fields.what: The risk level is the product of likelihood and impact, each scored 1–5, giving a relative scale of 1 to 25. RL drives prioritisation and the choice of response strategy.
fields.castor: R-07: likelihood 3 × impact 4 = risk level 12.

fields.what: Very low: under 5% chance. Low: 5–10%. Medium: 10–25%. High: 25–50%. Very high: over 50%. Percentages are indicative and must be customised per project.
fields.castor: Default percentages kept; assessors must cite the evidence behind each band.

fields.what: Graded by share of project budget affected plus baselines, milestones, stakeholders, reputation and capacity to react: Very low under 1%, Low 1–2%, Medium 2–5%, High 5–10%, Very high over 10%.
fields.castor: On €8.4 m: High = €420k–€840k affected, or several milestones lost.

fields.what: Green: risk level 2 or less. Yellow: risk level 3 to 16. Red: risk level 20 or above. Bands are indicative and must be customised for the project.
fields.who: PM proposes · PSC endorses · PO approves
fields.castor: Bands kept as printed; red risks trigger an extraordinary PSC within five working days.

fields.what: Appetite: level of risk the organisation will accept pursuing its objectives. Threshold: negotiated quantified impact limit beyond which risk is not tolerated. Tolerance: stakeholders' willingness, variable per person.
fields.who: Key stakeholders determine · PSC states · PO approves
fields.castor: PSC, 26 Jun 2026: appetite risk level ≤ 6, likelihood under 25%, loss under €168,000.

fields.what: Select the best response strategy and plan the actions that control the risk. Selection considers risk level, risk type, effect on objectives, and a cost/benefit analysis of the strategy.
fields.castor: Reduce chosen for R-07 after costing a full second architect at €190k.

fields.what: For threats: Avoid, Reduce, Transfer/Share, Accept. Acceptance is passive (monitor only) or active (develop a contingency plan). The guide adds Exploit, Enhance, Share, Accept for opportunities.
fields.castor: R-07 Reduce; the Treaty-ratification risk accepted actively with a contingency plan.

fields.what: Very high impact with high or very high likelihood: avoid or reduce immediately. Very high impact, very low likelihood: transfer/share. Low likelihood with very low impact: accept. All others: reduce.
fields.who: PM applies · PO approves the table
fields.castor: Table used unchanged; deviations must be justified in the PSC minutes.

fields.what: Each risk gets an owner accountable for implementing its response. Actions state activities, milestones, deliverables, target resolution date, resources and dependencies; the costliest ones enter the Project Work Plan.
fields.castor: R-07 owner Leonardo da Vinci (SP); its two actions are Work Plan tasks 4.6 and 4.7.

fields.what: Monitor implementation of response activities while scanning the environment for new risks and for changes in likelihood or impact of existing ones; update the Risk Log accordingly.
fields.castor: Risk Log revisited at every Project Follow-up Meeting and at each milestone review.

fields.what: PM identifies, assesses and monitors risks; new risks and changes are approved by the PO and reported to the PSC. A Risk Management Team may be appointed if needed.
fields.castor: Florence Nightingale approves new risks; no Risk Management Team — the PM plus Henry Gantt (PSO).

fields.what: Two rows: the Risk Management Plan (I, C, A, C, I, I, R, I) and the Manage Risks process (I, C, A, S/C, C, I, R, C).
fields.castor: PSC is Consulted, not merely Informed — unusual for a management plan.

fields.what: Techniques: desk reviews, questionnaires, interviews, brainstorming, workshops, risk checklists, assumption analysis. Tools: the Risk Management Plan, the Risk Log and the Likelihood/Impact Matrix.
fields.castor: Assumption analysis added specifically for the Treaty-ratification assumption.

fields.what: Three blocks: identification and description (ID, category, title, description, status, identified by, date); assessment (L, I, RL, owner, escalation); response (strategy, action details, target date, traceability).
fields.castor: PM² Risk Log used unchanged; 31 risks open at the RfE gate.

fields.what: Proposed (initial), Assessing, Waiting for Approval, Approved (risk possibility accepted), Rejected (not relevant), Closed (managed and no longer a risk to the project).
fields.castor: R-07 closed on 26 Oct 2027 — it had materialised and moved to the Issue Log.

fields.what: A 5×5 qualitative matrix combining likelihood and impact; cells are coloured by risk level band and each band suggests a response strategy. It supplements, not replaces, the Risk Log.
fields.castor: Matrix printed in every monthly PSC pack with each open risk plotted.

fields.what: Names the concrete identification activities for this project — desk reviews, interviews, team brainstorming, PSC meetings, user workshops, questionnaires, risk checklists, assumptions analysis — and the risk categories used.
fields.castor: Business Case and Charter risks are the starting point, extended by user workshops.

fields.what: Describes the assessment activities and tools, the likelihood and impact scale definitions, the risk level thresholds, and names the person who approves them.
fields.castor: Thresholds proposed by the PM, endorsed by the PSC, approved by Florence Nightingale.

fields.what: Risk level bands decide the approval layer: low levels at the Managing Layer, mid levels by the Project Owner, high levels by the PSC and other governance bodies.
fields.who: PM applies · PO owns the rule
fields.castor: RL ≤ 6 Managing Layer · RL 8–15 Florence Nightingale · RL ≥ 16 the PSC.

fields.what: Sets the type and frequency of control: the Risk Log is updated at least weekly after the Project Follow-up Meeting, with a status collection procedure before every PSC.
fields.who: PM controls · risk owners supply status
fields.castor: Weekly Risk Log update; deep review at Release 1, Release 2 and go-live.

fields.what: Weekly collection of new or changed risks; monthly PSC report on major risks; approval requests to the PO; yearly Project Progress Report; PSC told when a risk becomes an issue.
fields.castor: PSC of 12 Oct 2027 formally told that R-07 had become issue ISS-012.

fields.what: Cross-references the Project Handbook (high-level approach and escalation), the Communications Management Plan (who is told what, when) and the Issue Management Plan (risks that have occurred).
fields.castor: Handbook, Communications and Issue plans, all version 1.0 of 26 Jun 2026.

fields.what: Lists related documents by title, version, date and location: Handbook, Issue Management Plan, Communications Management Plan, Risk Log and the project folder.
fields.castor: 23.Risk_Log.CASTOR.xlsx in the ESM PSO project folder.

traps: RL = L × I on 1–5 scales: green ≤ 2, yellow 3–16, red ≥ 20.
Appetite is what you accept; threshold is a quantified limit; tolerance is personal sensitivity.
A risk that materialises becomes an issue and moves to the Issue Log.
The plan sets the scales and process; the Risk Log holds the actual risks.
Risk Management Plan is the only Management Plan where PSC = C, not I.
